en.title: Matrix Robot Transformation Commands
en.description:
Execute the commands swapRows r1 r2, swapColumns c1 c2, reverseRow r, reverseColumn c, and rotate90Clockwise. Indices are 0-based; a rotation turns the matrix 90 degrees clockwise and may change the number of rows and columns. Every command index is valid for the matrix at that moment. The original site's combined example had answers that did not match the commands, so this site recomputed them.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: This site's input: R C (1..100), followed by R lines each containing C integers in 0..10⁹, then q (1..100), followed by q lines of commands.
en.output: On the first line, output the number of rows and columns of the final matrix; then output the matrix row by row, with the elements of each row separated by spaces.
en.explanation: Example 1: rotating the 2×3 matrix clockwise produces a 3×2 matrix whose three rows are 4 1, 5 2, 6 3; the new dimensions 3 2 are output first.
hints: A swap exchanges the corresponding elements directly, a reverse reverses the corresponding row or column, and a rotation turns column j, read from bottom to top, into the new row j.
